title: Heartbeat SLO drift — diary
content:
High-level problem statement:

Over the last two weeks we've seen intermittent SLO drift on hosted-api endpoints during low-to-medium traffic windows (~50–300 qps). The pattern looks like 1–3 second p99 spikes every few minutes while p50/p95 stay fine. Hypothesis: an internal heartbeat/health-check or actor scheduler wake cycle is causing short stalls on worker threads which manifest strongly at p99 under certain cache/batching states.

Why this doc exists (notes to self):
- capture rapid experiments run on my laptop + staging cluster
- record configs, commands, quick raw results (so I can reproduce later)
- keep initial mitigation ideas and next steps in one place before formalizing a runbook

Environment snapshot:
- runtime: redwood-runtime v2.4.1 (local build from PR 4123)
- model: vicuna-13b-8k (quantized/int8 path used for these runs)
- infra: single A10G node (staging-fleet-a10g-07) behind k8s HPA; node config: 64GB RAM, 4 pod slots
- tracing: jaeger sampling=10% (full traces collected with --trace-local for a few runs)
- experiment harness: bench-runner v0.9 (internal), config YAMLs in /tmp/heartbeat-runs/

Quick reproduction commands (staging):
- start harness: ./bench-runner --config /tmp/heartbeat-runs/load-50-300.yaml --out /tmp/heartbeat-runs/results
- tail logs: kubectl logs -f deploy/redwood-runtime -n staging | grep "heartbeat"
- collect p99: jq '.latency.p99' /tmp/heartbeat-runs/results/summary.json

What I changed between runs:
- batch_window_ms: 4 vs 12 (smaller window reduces latency but may increase scheduling frequency)
- heartbeat_interval_ms: 5000 vs 15000 (this is the internal worker heartbeat I suspect)
- preemption: enabled vs disabled (k8s pod eviction-preemption prosthetics)
- kv_cache_mode: warm vs cold (warm means pre-populated KV caches)

Representative raw results (abbreviated) — all runs 30m steady with same synthetic prompt mix (mean token length 60):
- baseline (batch_window_ms=12, heartbeat=15000, cold cache): p50=28ms, p95=74ms, p99=1380ms, qps=120
- reduced-batch (batch_window_ms=4, heartbeat=15000, cold cache): p50=24ms, p95=68ms, p99=1120ms, qps=118
- heartbeat-short (batch_window_ms=4, heartbeat=5000, cold cache): p50=25ms, p95=80ms, p99=2100ms, qps=117
- heartbeat-short + warm-cache: p50=22ms, p95=60ms, p99=420ms, qps=122
- heartbeat-short + warm-cache + preemption-disabled: p50=22ms, p95=58ms, p99=390ms, qps=121

Observations / interpretation:
1) The p99 spikes correlate with shorter heartbeat intervals when the KV cache is cold. Short heartbeats + cold cache seems to coincide with big p99 regressions, suggesting the heartbeat triggers a work-stealing/wake path that forces a cache population step on a hot path.
2) Warm caches largely eliminate the giant p99 cliffs even when heartbeat is short. So the expensive operation (cache population) is the likely culprit.
3) Disabling preemption slightly helps but is not the dominant factor. Pod-level scheduling jitter contributes to noise but primary is the intra-process wake/populate behaviour.
4) Reducing batch window reduces some tail but doesn't remove large outliers. So batching helps amortize cost but doesn't eliminate it if the expensive op happens mid-request.

Trace excerpts:
- trace 2025-03-05T14:22:12Z (heartbeat-short cold): worker-23 blocked 1.9s at cpu:run_populate_kv_cache -> queuing -> resume
- trace suggests the populate operation runs on request path and acquires a global lock briefly (0.8–1.6s).

Immediate short-term mitigations tried (results above):
- pre-populate KV caches for recently used shards at startup (reduced p99 massively)
- increase heartbeat interval to 15s (less frequent wakes) — simpler but increases detection latency for unhealthy workers
- move populate_kv_cache to background worker thread (WIP patch in PR 4123) — promising in local tests, need staged rollout

Unresolved/risks:
- pre-populating caches increases memory footprint and has edge cases on autoscaling (cold nodes will still hit the path)
- increasing heartbeat makes detection slower; we need to measure MTTU (mean time to unhealthy) tradeoff and tune alongside liveness probe behaviour
- background-populate relies on non-blocking queue semantics; must ensure it does not introduce duplicate work or exacerbate thundering during recovery

Next experiments to run (ordered):
1) roll out background-populate patch to a 5% canary and run same 30m workload; instrument queue depth and double-check no dupe-populate logs
2) test heartbeat=10s (middle ground) with warm-cache and cold-cache cases to find knee point
3) synthetic failure injection: force KV populate to take 2s and measure impacts with various batching windows
4) instrument app-level metric gauge: "kv.populate.duration" with histogram buckets to drive alerting/paging thresholds

Run notes (timestamps):
- 2025-02-15 09:12 — baseline run, saw first p99 cliff (1.38s). Logged INF-987.
- 2025-02-19 16:00 — tried warm-cache boot; p99 reduced to ~420ms. Slacked findings to #sre-ops.
- 2025-03-05 14:10 — short-heartbeat run; reproduced 2.1s cliffs, collected full traces.
- 2025-03-18 11:04 — merged early background-populate prototype (PR 4123) into staging branch; local microbench improved.

Checklist / TODOs:
- [ ] Create monitoring dashboard widget for kv.populate.duration and kv.populate.count per node
- [ ] Add integration test that simulates cold cache populate under controlled arrival patterns (Poisson and burst)
- [ ] Draft temporary runbook guidance: increase heartbeat only for low-traffic nodes, prefer background-populate over heartbeat tuning
- [ ] Coordinate with product to understand acceptable MTTU change for Dedicated customers (SLA implications)

Notes to reviewers (Sofia/Liam):
- If you run the canary, please capture /tmp/heartbeat-runs/canary-*.json and upload. Critical: preserve traces with --trace-local for at least 5 of the p99 events.
- Watch memory growth on nodes with pre-population enabled; I saw a ~700MB increase on a10g nodes after 20m under qps=120.

Final thought (working hypothesis):
This is less a pure scheduling jitter issue and more a synchronous heavy path (kv.populate) that gets triggered by internal wake/heartbeat cycles. The most promising long-term fix is moving populate off the request handling critical path and using background/async strategies paired with smarter cache priming.

---
Quick paste of config used for most runs (sanitized):
---
workload:
  arrivals: poisson
  mean_qps: 120
  clients: 8
  token_mix: [short, medium, long]
runtime:
  batch_window_ms: 4
  heartbeat_interval_ms: 5000
  kv_cache_mode: cold
  preemption: enabled
---

If I don't return to this doc in a week: escalate to eng-sre lead and move PR 4123 up the queue.

Ian
(quick personal note: bring this to retro with SRE Friday slot — might be a good partner demo)
